$comment: Read by the dev-team plugin hooks (guard.mjs / watch.mjs). Patterns are case-insensitive regexes. deny = blocked, ask = the user must confirm. Environments: test = postgres-test (localhost:5433) · development = Neon branch 'development' (backend/.env, APP_ENV=development) · production = Neon branch 'production' (Fly secrets / secrets manager only). See TEAM.md → Hard rules.

bash.message: Port 5005 is the dev backend. Until backend/.env has been switched to the development branch (npm run env:set-dev-db, run by Nave) it talks to the REAL production database. Use the isolated e2e backend on 5006. After the switch this rule can be relaxed to 'ask'.
A Neon connection. Only the DEVELOPMENT branch may be used from here — never production. Confirm which database this command targets.
Only the isolated test DB (localhost:5433) may be opened with a SQL client.

Raw Prisma writes/Studio are blocked: they use whatever backend/.env points at. Use `npm run schema:sync` (test + development DBs) or `schema:test:push` / `schema:dev:push`. Production is changed ONLY by the approved release step of a deploy.
`.env` files hold real secrets (DB URLs, API keys). Do not read or copy them; `.env.example` / `.env.test.example` are fine.
This script moves a database password from the clipboard into backend/.env. Nave runs it himself, in his own terminal.
Approving a production schema change is yours alone: you review the plan and type its id yourself, in your own terminal. An agent never approves on your behalf.

This reads the REAL production schema (read-only) and needs the production URL, which should never be in this machine's everyday environment. Meant to be run by Nave at deploy time; confirm before running it from here.
Deploy goes to production (the release step applies an APPROVED schema change, if any). Only with Nave's explicit go-ahead in this session.
This deletes the postgres-test data volume (test data only, but it also wipes the schema; it is rebuilt by `npm run schema:test:push`).

files.message: Approval files are written only by `npm run schema:approve:prod`, run by Nave after he reviews the plan. An agent never creates, edits or deletes one.

watch.message: Schema changed. How it propagates: the development DB updates itself (container start / when this file changes, or `npm run schema:sync`); the test DB updates before every e2e run. PRODUCTION changes only at deploy, and ONLY if Nave approved this exact SQL: `PROD_DATABASE_URL=… npm run schema:plan:prod` (he runs it) → review → optional fix draft in backend/schema-fixes/<plan id>.pre.sql → `npm run schema:approve:prod` → commit the approval → deploy. Below is the plan against the DEVELOPMENT database. Advise Nave in Hebrew: explain what each 🟡/🔴 item means for production data, propose a concrete fix draft where one is suggested (you may write it to backend/schema-fixes/), and let him decide — never approve for him.

A fix draft changed. It runs FIRST, inside the same transaction as the planned SQL, and only after Nave approves the plan it belongs to. It must contain no <placeholders> (approve refuses otherwise), and it should be idempotent-safe and minimal.

Deploy configuration changed. Keep: the schema gate (`schema:gate:prod`) before any `fly deploy` in deploy.sh, `release_command` in backend/fly.toml, and the prisma/, scripts/ and schema-approvals/ copies in backend/Dockerfile — together they are what stops an unapproved schema change.
